S15.01.note: The bottom status bar item (tooltip "Code, click to change model", apps/extension-vscode/src/extension.ts) also shows the model name.
steps: Sign in and open the chat panel.
Look at the button at the right of the composer bottom bar. It shows "Auto" by default.
Pick a specific model (see S15.10) and look at the button again.
Compare the name on the button with the model the next message will use, as Expected says.
S15.01.where: Chat panel > bottom of the message box, the button that shows the model name (its tooltip is "Model"; it reads "Auto" by default)

S15.02.needs: a signed-in account or a provider key
S15.02.note: Headings in the chat list are built as "Your providers · <provider>" or "Managed Cloud · <provider>" and only appear for groups that have models.
steps: Click the model button at the bottom of the chat.
Read the group headings. Provider headings show a provider name such as "Anthropic" or "OpenAI".
Open Command Palette and run "Code: Select Model" and compare the provider headings there.
Check each model row sits under the provider that makes it, as Expected says.
S15.02.where: Chat panel > the model button at the bottom of the message box > group headings in the list (for example "Anthropic"); also Command Palette > Code: Select Model > the provider headings in the list

S15.04.note: The model button popover in the chat has no search box. Only the Command Palette list filters by typing.
steps: Open Command Palette and type "Code: Select Model", then press Enter.
Type part of a model name into the box at the top of the list.
Look at the list: it should narrow to matching rows by name.
Clear the box and check the full list comes back.
S15.04.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model (the list opens with a text box; type to filter)

labels.text: Picks the model for each message from the task, your plan and cost.

S15.08.needs: a signed-in account whose plan includes Auto
S15.08.note: The Auto list also has "Instant", "Best" and "Economy" variants shown as "Auto · <name>" rows.
steps: Click the model button at the bottom of the chat.
Choose the row "Auto" in the Recommended group.
Send a short message and check the model button still reads "Auto".
Compare with Expected: the product picks a model per message.
S15.08.where: Chat panel > model button at the bottom of the message box > row "Auto" under Recommended; also Command Palette > Code: Select Model > row "Auto"

S15.09.note: The default is saved only when no conversation exists (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts selectModel). How a tester reaches the no-conversation state in the UI was not confirmed from code.
steps: Close any open chat conversation, or use a fresh panel with no conversation.
Open Command Palette, run "Code: Select Model" and pick a model.
Read the message: it should say new chats now use that model.
Open Settings, search for agiWorkforce.model, and check the value is the chosen model.
S15.09.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model, with no chat conversation open (the picker then saves a default); the saved value is the setting Default LLM model

S15.10.needs: a signed-in account or a provider key with at least one reachable model
S15.10.note: The Select Model list only offers models the plan can use; locked rows open an upgrade or key prompt instead.
steps: Open Command Palette and run "Code: Select Model".
Pick a specific model row, for example one from a provider group.
Check the model button at the bottom of the chat now shows that model's name.
Send a message and check it runs on the chosen model, as Expected says.
S15.10.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model > pick a model row (not Auto); or the model button at the bottom of the chat

S15.11.note: The row text is built from catalog best-for phrases, so it is a short tag list, not a written description. The chat model button popover uses the same description text.
steps: Open Command Palette and run "Code: Select Model".
Read the description on each model row: it shows a plan line, best-use phrases, "Thinking" for thinking models and a speed word.
Read the detail line under a row for the model id and context limits.
Compare with Expected: each model has a short note of what it is good for.
S15.11.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model > the grey description text on each model row (the detail line shows the model id and limits)

steps: Open Command Palette and run "Code: Select Model".
Read the speed word on several rows, for example "Fastest", "Fast", "Medium speed" or "Slower".
Compare the words between models.
Check the faster and slower models show different words, as Expected says.
S15.16.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model > the speed word in the description of each model row

S15.17.note: Searched apps/extension-vscode for cost and usage text in the model list. The picker rows show plan, speed and capability only, not cost or usage. MODEL_COST_RATES in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/model-picker/modelConstants.ts feeds only the token counter in apps/extension-vscode/src/data/tokenCounter.ts. Turn cost appears only as a status bar message after a turn (apps/extension-vscode/src/data/turnUsage.ts), and the Model Dashboard (Code: Model Dashboard) shows requests and latency, not cost.

labels.text: Your plan uses Auto; upgrade your AGI plan to choose these models

S15.18.needs: a Free account or any account whose plan lacks some models
S15.18.note: The plan names come from billing plan labels in code, so the exact words depend on the plan catalog.
steps: Sign in with an account whose plan does not include every model (for example a Free account).
Open Command Palette and run "Code: Select Model".
Find the heading "Upgrade your AGI plan" and read the rows under it; each shows a lock icon and a line such as "<plan> plan and up".
Compare the plan named on each locked row with Expected: the plan that unlocks the model is shown.
S15.18.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model > the group heading "Upgrade your AGI plan" (locked rows sit under it); in the chat model button popover, a group with the text "Your plan uses Auto; upgrade your AGI plan to choose these models"

S15.22.needs: a reasoning-capable model (for example a thinking model on the plan)
S15.22.note: For a model without effort levels the group says "This model does not take a reasoning effort."
steps: Choose a reasoning-capable model (see S15.10).
Click the button with tooltip "Mode and reasoning effort".
Read the group "Reasoning effort" and its options (None, Minimal, Low, Medium, High, xHigh, Max).
Pick one level, send a message and check the choice applied, as Expected says.
S15.22.where: Chat panel > the button with tooltip "Mode and reasoning effort" at the bottom of the message box > group "Reasoning effort"; also Command Palette > Code: Set Reasoning Effort, and the "..." More actions menu > "Next message effort"

S15.27.needs: Ollama or LM Studio installed and running with a model loaded
S15.27.note: The local group is built only in the chat model popover (openModelPopover in ChatStateManager.ts). The Command Palette list was not confirmed to show local models.
steps: Start Ollama or LM Studio on this computer and load a model.
Click the model button at the bottom of the chat.
Look for the group "On this device" and the local model names in it.
Pick a local model, send a message and check the model button shows it, as Expected says.
S15.27.where: Chat panel > model button at the bottom of the message box > group "On this device"

S15.28.needs: your own provider API key (from that provider's console)
S15.28.note: The key is saved through the AGI CLI, and the list and its title are in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/capabilityManagement.ts.
steps: Open Command Palette and run "Code: Provider API Keys".
Pick a provider from the list and enter your own API key.
Read the confirmation: it says that provider's models are now under Your providers in the model picker.
Open the model button at the bottom of the chat and look for the "Your providers" group, as Expected says.
S15.28.where: Command Palette > Code: Provider API Keys > pick a provider > enter the key; then the model button at the bottom of the chat shows models under "Your providers"

S15.29.note: The value is saved to the global setting agiWorkforce.model. The package.json description mentions a shortcut cmd+shift+m, but no keybinding for agi-workforce.selectModel exists in package.json.
steps: Close any open conversation and run "Code: Select Model" from Command Palette.
Pick a model and confirm the message that new chats now use it.
Run Developer: Reload Window from Command Palette, or quit and reopen VS Code.
Open a new chat and check the model button shows the same model, as Expected says.
S15.29.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model (with no conversation open) > pick a model; then reload VS Code and open a new chat to see the model button

S15.30.note: The conversation scope is chosen when a conversation exists (ChatStateManager.ts selectModel). Confirm the exact way a conversation gets created before a tester starts.
steps: Open an existing chat that has at least one message (Sessions in the chat header opens the list).
Pick a different model from the model button or from Code: Select Model.
Read the message: it says this chat now uses that model and new chats still start with the default.
Click New chat and check the model button still shows the default, as Expected says.
S15.30.where: Open a chat that already has messages (Sessions button in the chat header) > model button or Command Palette > Code: Select Model > pick a different model

S15.34.needs: a chat on a model that can use tools or images, and a target model that cannot
S15.34.note: The check runs only from the Command Palette path (commandSetup.ts). Choosing a model from the chat model button does not show this dialog. The check also needs catalog metadata for both models.
steps: Use a chat on a model that can use tools or read images.
Open Command Palette and run "Code: Select Model".
Pick a model that lacks tools or image input, or has a smaller context window.

Read the modal dialog: it says Switch to <model>? and explains what is lost (for example it cannot read or edit files or run commands). Choose Switch anyway to confirm or cancel to stop, as Expected says.
S15.34.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model > pick a model that cannot use tools, cannot read images, or has a smaller context than the current model; a modal dialog appears with the button "Switch anyway"
